name: Violet (RYB)
lede: Violet (RYB) marks the violet point of the red-yellow-blue painter's color wheel, a teaching convention rather than a measured pigment, and matches [[vivid-violet]] exactly in our data.

sections.title: A wheel position, not a dye
sections.body:
RYB is the painter's primary-color wheel taught in classrooms; "Violet (RYB)" names the wheel's violet point rather than any specific paint [1]. Our data finds it an exact duplicate of [[vivid-violet]], 0.0 units apart [2]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary does not file this exact name [3]. Our library does record several neighboring names the dictionary filed at this hue: Basketball (block 205, Maerz and Paul 1930, first recorded 1916), Bishop's Violet (block 216, Maerz and Paul 1930, first recorded 1789) and Campanula Violet (block 205) [3].

Its nearest distinct look-alikes are [[purple-munsell]] (5.3 units, more vivid and lighter) and [[dark-violet]] (5.5, more vivid and lighter) [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color across at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed; a wheel-primary this saturated is rare in aged paint [5].
